top_story: Two years after Gaza’s war shifted into a nominal ceasefire-and-rebuild phase, reconstruction is hardening into a system of control as Israeli movement curbs continue to block treatment and drive cancer deaths to two to three times prewar levels. The humanitarian toll is not incidental to the political order emerging in the enclave; restrictions on access, aid, and mobility are shaping daily survival and eroding any credible path to recovery. In Syria, the court’s 11 August death sentence in absentia for Bashar al-Assad and Maher al-Assad signals a sharper push to codify wartime accountability after years in which mass violence outlasted meaningful justice. The wider regional picture is one in which postwar language—whether reconstruction or legal reckoning—masks how coercive power still determines who can live, move, and recover.
